papers.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Recent foundation models for single-cell transcriptomic data generate informative, context-aware gene and cell representations. Spatial transcriptomic (ST) data offer extra positional insights but were not considered by these single-cell models. We introduce stFormer, a transformer model tailored for ST data, which employs the cross-attention module to incorporate spatial ligand genes. To unify different ST technologies with a trade-off between resolution and gene coverage, we propose a biased cross-attention method that enables the model to do learning with single-cell resolution on whole-tra
papers.summary: stFormer is a transformer-based foundation model designed specifically for spatial transcriptomics data, using cross-attention to incorporate spatial ligand signaling genes into learned cell and gene representations. It introduces a biased cross-attention mechanism to unify different spatial transcriptomics platforms that vary in resolution and gene coverage, enabling single-cell-resolution learning on whole-transcriptome data. This addresses a gap where existing single-cell foundation models ignore spatial positional information.

papers.title: AcrSeek: Metric Learning with Hybrid Negative Mining for Anti-CRISPR Protein Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance.
papers.abstract: Anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are key targets for precise control of CRISPR-based genome editing and phage-host coevolution research. Their experimental identification is costly and low-throughput, so computational predictors are used to prioritise candidates for testing. In this setting validated positives number in the hundreds while phage-derived putative negatives reach tens of thousands, producing extreme class imbalance. Yet existing classification-based predictors train and evaluate on 1:1 balanced datasets and allow high-similarity sequences between trainin
papers.summary: AcrSeek is a computational tool for detecting anti-CRISPR (Acr) proteins, which inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity and are useful for controlling genome editing. Unlike prior predictors that train on artificially balanced datasets, AcrSeek uses metric learning with hybrid negative mining to handle the extreme class imbalance (hundreds of positives vs. tens of thousands of negatives) typical of real-world Acr discovery, while also addressing sequence similarity leakage between training and test sets.

papers.title: Post-Search Validation and Curation of Site-Resolved N‑Glycoproteomics Data.
papers.abstract: Given the significant role of glycosylation in modulating protein structure and activity, glycoproteomics is gaining increased interest from the broad scientific community. Large-scale site-resolved N-glycoproteomics relies on automated MS2-based searches, but candidate glycopeptide assignments can remain ambiguous when isomeric or isobaric glycan structures, adducts, chemical modifications, in-source fragments, or incomplete MS2 evidence support more than one plausible interpretation. Here, we systematically categorize common challenges and misassignments in glycoproteomics and present a post
papers.summary: This paper systematically catalogs common challenges and misassignments that arise in automated MS2-based site-resolved N-glycoproteomics, including ambiguities from isomeric/isobaric glycans, adducts, chemical modifications, and incomplete fragmentation evidence. It then presents a post-search validation and curation framework to help researchers distinguish correct glycopeptide assignments from plausible but incorrect alternatives.

papers.title: Lipid tail length dictates membrane disruption by carmofur analogs and reveals noncanonical modes of action.
papers.abstract: Carmofur, a lipidated urethane derivative and prodrug of 5-fluorouracil, has an established clinical application as an antineoplastic agent for the treatment of colorectal cancer, primarily through inhibition of acid ceramidase and subsequent intracellular drug release. Beyond this oncological application, recent drug repurposing efforts have identified covalent inhibition of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease as an additional antiviral mechanism. The pronounced amphiphilic character of carmofur, arising from a polar fluoropyrimidine headgroup appended to a hydrophobic aliphatic tail, raises the pos
papers.summary: This study examines how the length of the lipid tail in carmofur analogs affects their ability to disrupt membranes, revealing that tail length is a key determinant of membrane activity. The findings suggest that carmofur and its analogs may act through noncanonical mechanisms beyond their known targets, such as acid ceramidase inhibition or SARS-CoV-2 protease inhibition.

papers.title: CheckAMG: Accurate Identification of Auxiliary Viral Genes with Genome-Language Models.
papers.abstract: Viruses shape microbial metabolism through auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that reprogram host metabolism, physiology, and gene regulation during infection. Identifying AVGs is complicated by ambiguous viral versus cellular assignment, inconsistent curation, and reliance on sequence homology that misses divergent functions. Here we present CheckAMG, which pairs annotation-based AVG prediction, curated with a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic function, with a finetuned genome-language model for annotation-independent discovery. Benchmarked against DRAM-V and VIBRAN
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CheckAMG is a new tool for identifying auxiliary viral genes (AVGs) that combines annotation-based prediction with a fine-tuned genome-language model to detect divergent genes missed by homology methods. It uses a per-gene viral scoring system and ontological mapping of metabolic functions, and is benchmarked against existing tools DRAM-V and VIBRANT. The approach improves accuracy in distinguishing viral from cellular genes in metagenomic data.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Multitask Framework Integrating Habitat and Deep Learning for Predicting Early Disease Control and Survival in Immunotherapy-Treated Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients show heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study developed ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask network integrating CT-derived habitat and 2.5-dimensional (2.5D) deep learning features for simultaneously predicting early disease control (DC) and overall survival (OS). Of 1,234 patients with HCC enrolled from eight institutions and public databases, 832 ICI-treated patients were used for model development. ECOS-Net fused features using multi-head attention and generated early DC probabilities and OS risk scores. ECOS-DC a
papers.summary: This study introduces ECOS-Net, a transformer-based multitask deep learning framework that combines CT-derived habitat imaging features with 2.5D deep learning to simultaneously predict early disease control and overall survival in hepatocellular carcinoma patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors. Trained on 832 ICI-treated patients from eight institutions and public databases, the model aims to address heterogeneous treatment responses by providing integrated predictions from imaging data.

papers.title: Agentic campaign control for high-throughput de novo binder design.
papers.abstract: Progress in artificial intelligence has produced a rapidly growing ecosystem of methods for de novo protein design. With access to many specialized and often complementary tools, how does one use them effectively, especially with a finite compute budget? Here, we introduce Target-adaptive Rescue-Explore-eXploit (T-REX) , an agentic protein binder design framework that orchestrates multiple state-of-the-art protein generative models and structure evaluators. Over the course of a design campaign, T-REX leverages large language model (LLM) agents to reason over accumulating outcomes and decide wh
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: T-REX is an agentic framework that uses LLM agents to orchestrate multiple protein generative models and structure evaluators for de novo binder design, adaptively deciding which tools to run as results accumulate. It aims to make high-throughput binder design campaigns more effective under finite compute budgets by reasoning over outcomes and balancing exploration and exploitation.

papers.title: CardioChrom Reconstructs the Human Cardiac Virtual Epigenome from Single-Nucleus Transcriptomes.
papers.abstract: Matched epigenomic profiling remains scarce in human heart failure, limiting regulatory interpretation of single-nucleus ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing data. We developed CardioChrom, a cardiac-specialized framework that reconstructs chromatin accessibility, histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac), and histone H3 lysine 27 trimethylation (H3K27me3) from single-nucleus RNA profiles.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CardioChrom is a cardiac-specialized computational framework that reconstructs three epigenomic modalities—chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3—directly from single-nucleus RNA sequencing profiles of human heart tissue. This enables regulatory interpretation of single-nucleus transcriptomic data in heart failure, where matched epigenomic profiling is scarce.

papers.title: Combined Analysis of Transcriptome and Metabolome of Large-Size Triploid Rainbow Trout in Different Seasons.
papers.abstract: Seasonal temperature variation poses a significant physiological challenge for cold-water aquaculture species; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying seasonal adaptation in large-sized triploid rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated liver transcriptomics and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomics across four seasons (February, May, August, November) to investigate this phenomenon. Seasonal comparisons revealed pronounced molecular reprogramming, with the comparison between May and August showing the largest transcriptomic shift (13,359 di
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study integrated liver transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics in large triploid rainbow trout across four seasons to uncover molecular mechanisms of seasonal adaptation. The May-to-August comparison showed the largest transcriptomic shift, revealing pronounced seasonal molecular reprogramming in this cold-water aquaculture species.

papers.title: Self-supervised plasma proteomic representations for prospective disease prediction across varying protein availability.
papers.abstract: Large-scale plasma proteomics offers opportunities to characterize disease susceptibility and improve prospective risk prediction, but transferring proteomic predictors across datasets remains challenging because measured protein sets differ across cohorts, study phases and assay configurations. Here we developed a self-supervised protein-token Transformer that maps the proteins observed in each sample to a fixed-dimensional participant representation, allowing unavailable proteins to be omitted rather than imputed. Using plasma proteomic profiles from 53,014 participants in the UK Biobank Pha
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised Transformer model that converts plasma proteomic profiles into fixed-dimensional participant representations while naturally handling missing proteins across cohorts and assay configurations. Applied to 53,014 UK Biobank participants, this approach enables prospective disease risk prediction that transfers across datasets with differing protein panels, avoiding imputation. The method addresses a key barrier to reusing proteomic predictors in heterogeneous clinical and research settings.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure.
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files ra
papers.summary: dictyBase 2026 is a complete reimplementation of the Dictyostelium discoideum model organism database as a self-contained service built on static data files and minimal infrastructure. It continues to provide genomic data, protocols, stock center information, and community news for this widely used model organism, whose genes have human orthologs relevant to cancer and neurodegeneration research.

papers.title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI.
papers.abstract: In this work, we comprehensively evaluate three popular feature-extraction paradigms in AI-based neuroimaging modeling: (1) computation of anatomical surfaces and volumes, (2) supervised learning with convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and (3) unsupervised pretraining of vision transformer (ViT) foundation models, followed by supervised finetuning. Our study is based on 18 publicly available datasets containing 3D structural T1-weighted MRI scans from approximately 80,000 participants across seven distinct clinical tasks. We observe that a linear model based on anatomical features matches t
papers.summary: This study compares three approaches for extracting features from structural brain MRI scans—anatomical surface/volume measurements, supervised CNNs, and unsupervised pretrained ViT foundation models—across 18 public datasets and ~80,000 participants spanning seven clinical tasks. The authors find that a simple linear model built on anatomical features performs competitively with the more complex learned representations, suggesting that hand-crafted anatomical measures remain a strong baseline for neuroimaging AI.

papers.title: GeoEPred: A multimodal structure-aware geometric deep learning framework for Gram-negative bacterial secreted effector prediction with sequence semantics.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria is important for elucidating bacterial pathogenic mechanisms and developing precise anti-infective strategies. Although existing methods have benefited from the strong sequence feature extraction capacity of pretrained protein language models, reliance on linear sequence information alone often fails to fully capture the three-dimensional conformational signals required for virulence functions. Meanwhile, conventional structure-based methods are limited by the scarcity of experimentally resolved protein structures. To
papers.summary: GeoEPred is a multimodal deep learning framework that combines protein language model sequence embeddings with predicted 3D structural features to identify effector proteins secreted by Gram-negative bacteria. By integrating geometric deep learning over structures with sequence semantics, it aims to overcome the limitations of sequence-only and structure-only approaches, which respectively miss conformational signals and suffer from sparse experimental structures.

papers.title: Multiscale cross modal fusion and cascaded signal propagation for drug target interaction prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target interaction (DTI) facilitates the translation of lead compounds into clinical therapeutics. Despite progress in deep learning, two challenges remain: the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein modalities and insufficient use of complementary knowledge from pretrained encoders. To address these issues, we propose SF-DTI, a unified framework that integrates multi-encoder protein fusion, structure-semantic drug alignment, and progressive cross-modal refinement for DTI prediction. Specifically, SF-DTI captures global protein semantics from mult
papers.summary: The paper introduces SF-DTI, a deep learning framework for predicting drug-target interactions that combines multiple protein encoders, aligns drug structures with their semantic representations, and progressively refines cross-modal features. It aims to bridge the representation gap between heterogeneous drug and protein data and better exploit pretrained encoders, improving DTI prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding for anticancer peptide prediction via transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Computational identification of anti-tumor peptides (ACPs) is challenged by limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences. Standard transformer positional encodings fail to capture the periodicities and local motifs that govern peptide function. We propose dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), which replaces fixed sinusoidal encodings with parallel adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches, fused by a context-aware gating mechanism. A dual-stage transfer learning strategy pre-trains on 5,785 curated peptide sequences before fine-tuning on ACP74
papers.summary: The authors introduce dynamic Fourier wavelet positional encoding (DFWPE), a transformer positional encoding scheme that combines adaptive Fourier and multi-scale wavelet branches via context-aware gating to better capture periodicities and local motifs in peptide sequences. They pair this with a dual-stage transfer learning strategy, pre-training on 5,785 curated peptides before fine-tuning for anticancer peptide prediction. The approach aims to overcome limited training data and the multi-scale nature of biological sequences.

papers.title: Machine learning-assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco.
papers.abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) is foundational to life on Earth, catalyzing carbon dioxide (CO2) fixation to generate biomass. However, Rubisco is a slow and inefficient enzyme that has proven challenging to engineer. We applied the structure-informed machine learning (ML) model ESM-IF1 to identify plausible amino acid sites in the large subunit of Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco to target for directed evolution. ML-assisted library design followed by selection in Rubisco-dependent Escherichia coli identified multiple enriched variants displaying improved catalytic efficie
papers.summary: This study used the structure-informed machine learning model ESM-IF1 to guide directed evolution of the large subunit of tobacco Rubisco, identifying amino acid sites for targeted mutagenesis. Selection in Rubisco-dependent E. coli yielded variants with improved catalytic efficiency, demonstrating that ML-assisted library design can overcome the engineering challenges of this notoriously inefficient enzyme. The work highlights a practical route to improving CO2 fixation in plants.

papers.title: Pretrained spectrum representations for diverse tandem mass spectrometry proteomics tasks.
papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry is the dominant technology in the field of proteomics, enabling high-throughput analysis of the protein content of complex biological samples. Due to the complexity of the instrumentation and resulting data, sophisticated computational methods are required for the processing and interpretation of acquired mass spectra. Machine learning has shown great promise to improve the analysis of mass spectrometry data, with numerous purpose-built methods for improving specific steps in the data acquisition and analysis pipeline reaching widespread adoption. Each of these tasks rely on
papers.summary: This paper introduces pretrained spectrum representations that can be applied across diverse tandem mass spectrometry proteomics tasks, rather than building separate models for each step. By learning general-purpose embeddings of mass spectra, the approach aims to improve multiple downstream analyses such as peptide identification and quality control. The work represents a step toward foundation-model-style transfer learning in proteomics.

papers.title: A self-supervised foundation model for large-scale zebrafish image analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput zebrafish screening generates large volumes of imaging data, creating a need for scalable computational methods that reduce dependence on manual annotation and repeated task-specific model development. In this study, we develop a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis pretrained on more than 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous zebrafish imaging datasets spanning different developmental stages, imaging platforms, modalities, and experimental conditions. By learning a shared representation from diverse unlabeled zebrafish images, the proposed framework
papers.summary: The authors developed a self-supervised foundation model for zebrafish image analysis, pretrained on over 468,000 images from seven heterogeneous imaging datasets covering different developmental stages, platforms, and modalities. By learning a shared representation from unlabeled images, the framework aims to reduce reliance on manual annotation and task-specific model development for high-throughput zebrafish screening.

papers.title: Explainable AI-driven marker selection and development of EastFocus AISNPplex 61 assay for fine-scale biogeographical ancestry inference.
papers.abstract: A hierarchical ancestry inference framework was developed to resolve continental and fine-scale East Asian population structures for forensic applications. Combining the shapley additive explanations (SHAP) method with recursive feature elimination, 58 ancestry informative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (AIM-SNPs) were selected. A self-developed 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex system (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) was established, integrating these AIM-SNPs, two Y-chromosomal InDels, and the Amelogenin locus. Validation demonstrated reliable single-source genotyping down to 250-500 pg and full
papers.summary: This study developed a hierarchical ancestry inference framework that uses explainable AI (SHAP combined with recursive feature elimination) to select 58 ancestry-informative SNPs for resolving fine-scale East Asian population structure. These markers were incorporated into a 6-dye allele-specific PCR multiplex assay (EastFocus AISNPplex 61) alongside Y-chromosomal InDels and Amelogenin, with validation showing reliable genotyping from 250-500 pg of DNA. The work provides a forensically validated tool for biogeographical ancestry inference at fine scales.

papers.title: Time Series Segmentation in Adaptive Optics Ophthalmoscopy With Application to Flicker-Induced Vasodilation.
papers.abstract: To develop an automated image processing pipeline to segment retinal arterial walls in a series of adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, overcoming difficulties related to various quality levels within the series, to accurately evaluate morphometric differences.
papers.summary: This paper presents an automated image processing pipeline that segments retinal arterial walls across time-series adaptive optics ophthalmoscopy (AOO) images, addressing variable image quality within the series. The method is applied to evaluate flicker-induced vasodilation, enabling accurate morphometric measurements of vessel changes over time.

papers.title: Snail shell-derived hydroxyapatite on ant clay: a sustainable solution for phosphate sequestration and circular agricultural reuse.
papers.abstract: In this study, a sustainable adsorbent comprising hydroxyapatite derived from snail shells and clay collected from ant nests was developed and used for the efficient removal of phosphate (PO4 3-) from aqueous solutions. The synthesized adsorbent was characterized using different characterization techniques like FTIR spectroscopy, XRD, SEM, TGA, PZC, and BET analysis to confirm its successful synthesis, morphology, thermal stability, surface charges, and surface area, respectively. The adsorbent was systematically investigated for phosphate adsorption by optimizing key experimental parameters,
papers.summary: This study develops a sustainable phosphate adsorbent by combining hydroxyapatite extracted from snail shells with clay from ant nests, offering a low-cost way to remove phosphate from water. The material was characterized and optimized for phosphate uptake, supporting circular agricultural reuse of waste-derived materials.

papers.title: Integrative multiomics and machine learning identify uridine as a candidate modulator of MMP7-mediated immune cell infiltration in pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrosing interstitial lung disease (ILD) characterized by immune cell infiltration and extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition. Effective therapies remain limited. Uridine is an endogenous nucleoside with pro-reparative and immunomodulatory effects, but its molecular targets and immune mechanisms in IPF remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multiomics data with machine learning to identify uridine as a potential modulator of MMP7-mediated immune cell infiltration in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The work suggests uridine may influence immune mechanisms relevant to IPF pathology, offering a new candidate for therapeutic exploration.

papers.title: Serum Protein Panel Facilitates Surgical Decision-Making for Barcelona Stage B Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop a serum proteomic-based prognostic model for predicting surgical outcomes in BCLC stage B hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients, addressing the clinical heterogeneity that limits uniform treatment recommendations.
papers.summary: This study develops a serum proteomic-based prognostic model to predict surgical outcomes for patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage B hepatocellular carcinoma, a group with heterogeneous clinical presentations that complicates uniform treatment recommendations. The panel aims to help clinicians decide which stage B patients would benefit from surgery.

papers.title: ParaEM: Antigen-aware sequence-based paratope prediction with Expectation-Maximization.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of antibody paratopes-the residues contacting the antigen-is vital for understanding antibody-antigen recognition, antibody engineering, and vaccine design. However, structure-based predictors require antibody structural inputs, which are often obtained from experimentally determined antibody-antigen complexes in benchmark settings but are generally unavailable for new sequences. Conversely, sequence-based predictors scale efficiently but remain largely antigen-agnostic, limiting their use of pair-specific antigen context.
papers.summary: ParaEM is a new sequence-based method for predicting antibody paratopes (the residues that contact antigen) that incorporates antigen sequence context, unlike prior sequence-based tools that are antigen-agnostic. It uses an Expectation-Maximization framework to make paratope predictions without requiring antibody structure inputs, which are typically unavailable for new sequences.

papers.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning.
papers.abstract: Proteins are the main drivers of cell function and disease, making proteomics a powerful technique for biomarker discovery and defining cell identity. While current technologies can profile thousands of proteins and reach single-cell sensitivity, limited throughput restricts applications such as robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts. To close this gap, we present a deep-learning (DL) approach for the direct analysis of mass spectrometric (MS) data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity. Specifically, we introduce the ProFormer, a transformer pipeline that clas
papers.summary: ProFormer is a transformer-based deep learning pipeline that directly classifies mass spectrometry proteomics data, assigning proteomic profiles to sample identity without requiring traditional feature engineering. It is designed to work across both single-cell and plasma proteomes, aiming to enable robust classification of large biological or clinical cohorts despite limited throughput in current proteomics technologies.

papers.title: Discovery and biological characterization of 1-[4-(2-difluoromethoxyphenyl)-5-methylthiazol-2-yl]-3-(naphthalen-1-yl)urea (DFMNTU): A novel thiazolyl-urea chemotype targeting yellow fever virus and host casein kinase 2 (CK2).
papers.abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a re- emerging mosquito- borne flavivirus that causes severe hemorrhagic fever with high case- fatality rates. Due to vaccine contraindications, incomplete immunization coverage, and the absence of approved specific antivirals, host- directed drug discovery targeting cellular machinery exploited by YFV is a critical therapeutic priority. Here, 1-[4-(2- difluoromethoxyphenyl)- 5- methylthiazol- 2- yl]- 3-(naphthalen- 1- yl)urea (DFMNTU) was synthesized, characterized by NMR, MS, and HPLC, and evaluated for antiviral efficacy against YFV strain 17 D in Vero cells. DFM
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis and characterization of DFMNTU, a novel thiazolyl-urea compound that targets yellow fever virus (YFV) by inhibiting the host protein casein kinase 2 (CK2). The compound showed antiviral activity against YFV strain 17D in cell culture, suggesting a host-directed therapeutic strategy for a virus with no approved antivirals.

papers.title: pLM-HP: Peptide hormone prediction using pre-trained protein language model representations.
papers.abstract: Peptide hormones play key roles in metabolic regulation, growth and development, and the maintenance of homeostasis and are important targets for drug discovery and design. However, traditional experimental methods for screening and identifying peptide hormones are costly and inefficient. Although existing machine learning methods have made some progress, they pay limited attention to class imbalance, and there is still room to improve prediction performance.
papers.summary: The paper introduces pLM-HP, a machine learning method that uses representations from a pre-trained protein language model to predict peptide hormones. It explicitly addresses class imbalance, a common issue in this prediction task, and reports improved performance over existing methods. The tool aims to speed up identification of peptide hormones relevant to drug discovery.

papers.title: Screening for patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis via electronic health records: A multicenter machine learning development and validation study.
papers.abstract: Timely detection is crucial to improve outcomes in patients with cardiac amyloidosis (CA) by initiation of guideline-directed disease-modifying treatments. Although confirmatory bone scintigraphy is highly accurate for CA detection, identifying at-risk patients for referral remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, using structured multimodal electronic health record (EHR) data to guide referrals for confirmatory scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. Consecutive all-comer patients (n = 11,616) referred for bone scintigraphy at
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed and validated a machine learning model, Amylo-Detect, that uses structured multimodal electronic health record data to identify patients at risk for cardiac amyloidosis who should be referred for confirmatory bone scintigraphy and monoclonal protein testing. The model was trained on 11,616 consecutive patients referred for bone scintigraphy, aiming to improve timely detection and enable guideline-directed disease-modifying treatment.

papers.title: A serum proteomics-based predictive model for steroid-resistant immune checkpoint inhibitor associated myocarditis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICIAM) is one of the immune-related adverse events (irAEs) with low incidence but extremely high mortality. High-dose glucocorticoid pulse therapy remains the recommended initial treatment for patients with ICIAM. However, an inadequate response to corticosteroid therapy is observed in some patients, who are subsequently classified as having steroid-resistant immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (srICIAM). Early combination of second-line immunosuppression may represent an effective therapeutic strategy. However, Biomarkers capa
papers.summary: This study develops a serum proteomics-based predictive model to identify cancer patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis who will not respond to high-dose steroid therapy. Early identification of these steroid-resistant cases could enable timely addition of second-line immunosuppressive treatment, potentially improving outcomes in this highly fatal condition.

papers.title: Discovery of PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products through machine learning and structure-based screening.
papers.abstract: PIM-1 kinase, a serine/threonine kinase implicated in several cancers, has emerged as a promising yet underexplored target for anticancer therapy. This study aimed to identify the potential of PIM-1 inhibitors from marine natural products by integrating machine learning (ML)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling with structure-based virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study combines machine learning-based QSAR modeling with structure-based virtual screening to identify potential PIM-1 kinase inhibitors from marine natural products. PIM-1 is an anticancer target, and the work demonstrates a hybrid computational pipeline for drug discovery from natural product libraries.

papers.title: Progeny Differentiation in Faba Bean Using Hyperspectral Images and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Though currently a minor crop, faba bean is a promising source of plant-based protein as global diets shift towards more plant-based nutrition. To realize this potential, advances in breeding and cultivation are crucial. To exploit heterosis, faba bean breeding frequently utilizes synthetic cultivars, produced by open pollination of inbred lines, resulting in a mixture of F1 hybrid seeds and self-pollinated offspring. Pure F1 hybrid cultivars are currently unavailable due to unstable cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) systems. An ability to distinguish F1 seeds from their parental inbreds based
papers.summary: This study uses hyperspectral imaging combined with machine learning to distinguish F1 hybrid seeds from self-pollinated offspring in faba bean breeding. The approach could help breeders identify true hybrids in synthetic cultivars, where unstable cytoplasmic male sterility currently prevents pure F1 cultivar production. This supports more efficient exploitation of heterosis in faba bean as a plant-based protein crop.

papers.title: Information Leakage in Enzyme Substrate Prediction.
papers.abstract: Enzymes are essential catalysts in many cellular processes. Understanding their interactions with small molecules, such as regulators, cofactors, and most importantly, substrates, is crucial for understanding the biochemical processes that occur in cells. Correctly interpreting the roles of small molecules that interact with enzymes is key to elucidating enzyme function. Recently, enzyme-small molecule interaction prediction has attracted growing interest from computational methods, especially deep learning. As a result, researchers have published several datasets and numerous models with rema
papers.summary: This paper investigates information leakage in deep learning models for predicting enzyme-substrate interactions, a problem that can artificially inflate performance metrics. The authors likely demonstrate how data splitting or feature construction can leak test information into training, leading to overoptimistic results. They provide guidance on avoiding such pitfalls to ensure fair evaluation in computational enzyme function prediction.

papers.title: Progressive remodeling of global protein interaction networks in a mouse model of tauopathy.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative disease is marked not just by loss of proteins or cells, but by dynamic rewiring of macromolecular interaction networks that precede and drive pathology. Here, we present a temporally resolved, systems-scale map of multi-protein complex remodeling in a tauopathy model, integrating co-fractionation mass spectrometry, quantitative phosphoproteomics, and machine learning to decode phosphorylation-dependent shifts in protein interactomes across disease progression. This interactomic atlas serves as a resource to investigate functional assemblies, including MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-
papers.summary: This study maps how protein interaction networks progressively rewire over time in a mouse model of tauopathy, using co-fractionation mass spectrometry, phosphoproteomics, and machine learning. The authors generate a temporal interactomic atlas revealing phosphorylation-dependent shifts in multi-protein complexes, including specific assemblies like MAPT-Dpysl2 and Cyfip1-containing complexes, that precede and accompany disease pathology.

papers.title: Beyond affinity: AI-supported developability assessment and multi-objective optimization in antibody development.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic antibodies are a major class of medicines, but high target affinity alone does not ensure manufacturability, stability, safety, or clinical success. Developability has therefore become a central constraint in antibody engineering and has pushed the field beyond affinity-first screening toward multi-objective decision-making. Machine-learning-based models increasingly integrate antibody sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to estimate properties such as affinity, specificity, aggregation, viscosity, solubility, stability, immunogenicity, and pharmacokinetics before exper
papers.summary: This review argues that therapeutic antibody development must move beyond affinity-first screening to multi-objective optimization of developability properties like stability, solubility, and immunogenicity. It surveys how machine-learning models integrate sequence, structure, interaction, and assay data to predict these properties before experimental testing.

papers.title: A dual-tower multimodal framework with feature quality enhancement for predicting pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Pathological complete response (pCR) is a key endpoint following neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) in breast cancer, with potential to guide treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation. However, limited generalizability across institutions remains a major challenge due to heterogeneous imaging protocols (scanner vendors, field strengths, and acquisition parameters) and diverse patient populations, which can cause significant domain shifts in model performance. This study develops and externally validates a multimodal framework for post-neoadjuvant, preoperative prediction of pCR using multipa
papers.summary: This study develops a dual-tower multimodal deep learning framework that integrates imaging and clinical data to predict pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer patients. The framework includes a feature quality enhancement module designed to mitigate domain shifts caused by heterogeneous imaging protocols across institutions, and it is externally validated in a multicenter setting. The approach aims to improve generalizability and support treatment adaptation and surgical de-escalation decisions.

papers.title: Omics data discovery agents: Agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g., protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs lar
papers.summary: The authors present an agentic framework that uses AI agents to retrieve, reanalyze, and synthesize published omics data from the biomedical literature. The system addresses the problem that most published omics data remain functionally inaccessible because essential information is scattered across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories. This work aims to make published omics data more reusable for computational analysis.

papers.title: Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer: A Novel Approach for Multi-Objective De Novo Drug Design.
papers.abstract: Designing novel molecules that simultaneously satisfy several, often conflicting, properties is a long-standing challenge in drug design. While recent deep learning advances optimize single targets effectively, navigating the trade-offs required for multiple objectives remains a difficult problem.
papers.summary: The paper introduces the Multi-Objective-Conditioned-Return-Blocks Decision Transformer (MOC-RB-DT), a deep learning architecture for de novo drug design that aims to generate molecules satisfying multiple, often conflicting, properties simultaneously. It adapts the Decision Transformer framework with return-block conditioning to navigate multi-objective trade-offs, addressing a key limitation of existing single-target optimization methods.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of mitochondrial proteomes across the tree of life.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria arose from the endosymbiosis of a bacterium with an archaea-related host cell about 2 billion years ago. To understand their origins and evolution, we compared experimentally defined mitoproteomes from the MitoCarta Tree of Life project. Across eight organisms, we identified 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins within 3,199 families, of which 43% lack Pfam domains. We report 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens yet absent in humans, representing promising candidate targets for protozoan infectious diseases. Leveraging our experimentally defined mitoproteomes, we
papers.summary: This study compares experimentally defined mitochondrial proteomes across eight organisms spanning the tree of life, identifying 8,619 distinct mitochondrial proteins grouped into 3,199 families, with 43% lacking known Pfam domains. The authors highlight 33 protein families conserved in eukaryotic pathogens but absent in humans, offering potential drug targets for protozoan infectious diseases. The work provides a broad evolutionary resource for understanding mitochondrial origins and function.

papers.title: Integrating Multimodal MRI Habitat and Transformer-Based Pathomics to Predict High-Risk Molecular Subtypes and Explore Biological Mechanisms in Adult Diffuse Gliomas.
papers.abstract: This study aims to achieve accurate prediction of high-risk molecular subtypes of gliomas through a cross-scale Combined model, matching the model's classification metrics with patient risk stratification and exploring the underlying biological mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study develops a cross-scale combined model that integrates multimodal MRI-based tumor habitat imaging with transformer-based pathomics to predict high-risk molecular subtypes in adult diffuse gliomas. The model's classification performance is linked to patient risk stratification, and the authors explore the underlying biological mechanisms associated with the predicted subtypes.

papers.title: Autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease: a matched cross-sectional analysis of disease-specific associations in Qatari primary care.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune disorders have been linked to increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, but it is unclear whether the association is uniform across conditions or is concentrated in specific diseases, and whether inflammatory markers add value in a Middle Eastern primary-care setting. We examined disease-specific associations between autoimmune disorders and recorded CVD, rather than building a prognostic prediction tool.
papers.journal: American heart journal plus : cardiology research and practice
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether the link between autoimmune disorders and cardiovascular disease varies by specific autoimmune condition in a Qatari primary-care population. Using matched analysis, the authors assessed disease-specific associations and whether inflammatory markers add predictive value, rather than developing a prognostic tool.

papers.title: Combating antimicrobial resistance through multimodal data via artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical global health challenge, leading to substantial mortality and economic losses without science-based interventions. Conventional approaches to combating AMR have important limitations in addressing this escalating threat. Recent advances in AI, including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models, provide new opportunities to integrate multimodal data for AMR research. However, evidence remains uneven, with many approaches limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation. Here, we critically review AI
papers.summary: This review critically examines how artificial intelligence—including deep learning, large language models, and protein language models—can integrate multimodal data to combat antimicrobial resistance. It highlights that while these approaches offer new opportunities, much of the evidence remains limited to computational benchmarking rather than real-world validation.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning models for predicting New-onset acute organ injury within 48 hours of admission in patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Community-acquired acute cholangitis (CAAC) can progress to acute organ injury (AOI), increasing poor prognosis risk. This study aimed to develop machine learning models using clinical information obtained before AOI onset to predict new-onset AOI within 48 h after admission in patients with CAAC.
papers.summary: This study develops interpretable machine learning models that use routinely collected clinical data available at admission to predict which patients with community-acquired acute cholangitis will develop new acute organ injury within 48 hours. The goal is to enable earlier risk stratification and timely intervention in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Benchmarking hyperparameter optimization strategies for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genomic prediction has become an important approach for accelerating crop breeding by using genome-wide marker information to predict complex traits. However, the performance of genomic prediction models is influenced not only by model selection but also by hyperparameter optimization strategies, which have received limited attention in crop genomic prediction studies. Based on four crop datasets, including maize, rice, wheat, and foxtail millet, we evaluated the prediction performance and computational efficiency of six representative genomic prediction models under four hyperparameter optimi
papers.summary: This study benchmarks six genomic prediction models across four crop datasets (maize, rice, wheat, foxtail millet) to evaluate how different hyperparameter optimization strategies affect prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. The authors find that the choice of hyperparameter optimization strategy can meaningfully influence model performance, highlighting an often-overlooked factor in crop genomic prediction pipelines.

papers.title: Multi-omics graph attention network reveals neuro-immune-tumor pathways in breast cancer liver depression syndrome.
papers.abstract: Liver depression syndrome (LDS) is a core Chinese medicine (CM) syndrome implicated in the onset and progression of breast cancer, whose molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood, hindering further investigation.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-omics graph attention network to investigate the molecular mechanisms linking liver depression syndrome (LDS), a core Chinese medicine syndrome, to breast cancer progression. The approach integrates multiple omics layers to identify neuro-immune-tumor pathways associated with LDS, offering a systems-level view of how this syndrome may influence cancer biology.

papers.title: Exploratory radiomics analysis of T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI in relation to Parkinson's disease motor subtypes.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease motor subtypes, tremor-dominant (TD) and postural instability/gait difficulty (PIGD), differ in disease trajectory and prognosis, yet their classification depends on MDS-UPDRS-based clinical ratings that are susceptible to inter-rater variability and medication state.
papers.summary: This study applies exploratory radiomics analysis to T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI scans to investigate whether imaging features can distinguish between Parkinson's disease motor subtypes (tremor-dominant vs. postural instability/gait difficulty). The work aims to address limitations of current clinical rating-based subtyping, which is subject to inter-rater variability and medication effects. As an exploratory analysis, it assesses the potential of MRI-derived radiomic features as objective biomarkers for motor subtype classification.

papers.title: Efficacy and exploratory treatment-response modeling of acupuncture for acute migraine based on DIA proteomics: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: According to estimates from the 2019 Global Burden of Disease (GBD) study, approximately 1.1 billion people worldwide suffer from migraine, with a prevalence rate of about 14% to 15%. Despite the development of various medications for different types of migraine, such as acetaminophen and caffeine combination preparations, most patients still experience suboptimal symptom control. Therefore, identifying effective and safer alternative treatments holds significant clinical importance. Acupuncture was formally recommended by the World Health Organization as a migraine therapy as early as 1979. I
papers.summary: This is a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial testing whether acupuncture effectively treats acute migraine, using DIA (data-independent acquisition) proteomics to explore treatment-response biomarkers. The trial aims to link proteomic changes to clinical outcomes, potentially identifying molecular signatures that predict or reflect acupuncture response. As a protocol, no results are yet reported.

papers.title: Exploring the key genes of colorectal "adenoma-cancer" based on graph transformer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most lethal malignancies worldwide, and the precise identification of biomarkers from colonic adenoma to cancer is of great significance for preventing the development of adenocarcinoma. Given that existing methods inadequately capture the topological network relationships among genes, this study proposes a graph neural network model based on multifeature learning, named ChebTs, to investigate the correlation between key genes involved in the colorectal "adenoma-cancer" transition. The GSE41657 and GSE31905 datasets from the GEO database were stratified in
papers.summary: This study introduces ChebTs, a graph transformer-based neural network model that integrates multiple feature types to identify key genes driving the transition from colorectal adenoma to cancer. Using GEO datasets GSE41657 and GSE31905, the authors leverage gene network topology to pinpoint biomarkers that may help prevent adenocarcinoma development. The work demonstrates how graph-based deep learning can capture gene-gene relationships that conventional methods miss.

papers.title: Mechanism-aware and safety-validated AI for drug repurposing: a critical review and translational pharmacology framework.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted drug repurposing seeks to identify new therapeutic applications for existing drugs. Nevertheless, most of the existing studies are centered on prediction scores and candidate ranking, and there is still relatively little attention paid to the pharmacological mechanisms, safety and translational validation.
papers.summary: This critical review argues that most AI-driven drug repurposing studies focus narrowly on prediction scores and candidate ranking while neglecting pharmacological mechanism, safety, and translational validation. The authors propose a translational pharmacology framework that integrates mechanism-aware modeling and safety validation to make AI repurposing more clinically actionable.

papers.title: From surveillance to intelligence: a scoping review of machine learning for antimicrobial resistance surveillance intelligence across One Health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a leading global health threat requiring coordinated surveillance across human, animal, environmental, and genomic systems. Machine learning is increasingly applied to AMR data, yet its contribution to actionable surveillance intelligence, rather than prediction alone, remains poorly defined.
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how machine learning is being applied to antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance data across human, animal, environmental, and genomic domains within a One Health framework. It argues that most current ML efforts focus on prediction rather than generating actionable surveillance intelligence, and it maps the gap between predictive modeling and real-world decision support for AMR monitoring.

papers.title: Surveillance-Driven Machine Learning for Prediction of Antimicrobial Susceptibility: An Explainable Modeling Framework using the Pfizer ATLAS Dataset (2004 - 2023).
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing global public health threat, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where delayed antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) and limited diagnostic capacity complicate timely treatment and antimicrobial stewardship (AMS). Although large-scale surveillance programmes routinely collect antimicrobial susceptibility data, these datasets remain underutilised for predictive analytics.
papers.summary: This study develops an explainable machine learning framework to predict antimicrobial susceptibility using 20 years of surveillance data from the Pfizer ATLAS dataset (2004-2023). The approach aims to support antimicrobial stewardship and treatment decisions, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where rapid susceptibility testing is often unavailable. By leveraging routinely collected surveillance data for predictive analytics, the work demonstrates an underutilized resource for addressing antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: GP-DHT: A dual-head transformer with supervised contrastive learning for shared-gene pretraining and single-cell GRN prediction.
papers.abstract: Gene Regulatory Networks (GRNs) are crucial for understanding cell fate decisions and disease mechanisms. However, inferring GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing remains challenging due to noise, data sparsity, and species-specific distribution variations. We propose GP-DHT (Gene Pair-Dual Head Transformer), a single-cell GRN inference framework that pre-trains gene representations on a unified shared gene space using the BEELINE datasets of humans and mice. It models gene-cell expression relationships through a multi-relational heterograph and predicts transcription factor (TF)-target regulat
papers.summary: GP-DHT is a dual-head transformer framework that uses supervised contrastive learning to pretrain gene representations on a unified human-mouse shared gene space, then predicts transcription factor-target regulatory relationships from single-cell RNA-seq data. It models gene-cell expression via a multi-relational heterograph to address noise, sparsity, and cross-species distribution shifts in GRN inference. The approach is evaluated on BEELINE benchmark datasets.

papers.title: Radiomics and deep learning for immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes: imaging-derived immune phenotyping and clinical translation across solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple solid tumors, but durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients and conventional size-based imaging does not fully capture immune-related response patterns. Radiomics and deep learning offer a route to convert routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT into quantitative biomarkers of tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response. This narrative review critically synthesizes the evidence across solid tumors with an emphasis on four questions that are often separated in the literature: what
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on using radiomics and deep learning to predict immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes across solid tumors, framing imaging as a tool for non-invasive immune phenotyping. It emphasizes four interconnected questions often treated separately in the literature, covering tumor phenotype, whole-body heterogeneity, and temporal treatment response from routine CT, MRI, and PET/CT. The review aims to bridge methodological advances with clinical translation for patient selection and response monitoring.

papers.title: Explainable growth stage classification of cacao (Theobroma cacao L.) leaves and key feature visualization using vision transformer and transfer learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate and objective plant phenotyping is crucial for optimizing agricultural practices, understanding plant development, and enabling rapid responses to environmental changes. Traditional methods, often relying on visual observation, can be subjective, time-consuming, and may overlook subtle but important differences. This study demonstrates the power of combining digital imaging with deep learning to classify plant material with high accuracy, even when visual differences are minimal. We focused on differentiating between stage D (light green) and stage E (dark green) leaves of cacao (Theo
papers.summary: This study applies a vision transformer with transfer learning to classify cacao leaves into two developmental stages (D and E) based on subtle color differences, achieving high accuracy where visual inspection is unreliable. The authors also visualize key features driving the model's decisions, improving interpretability. The work demonstrates how deep learning can support objective, automated plant phenotyping in agricultural settings.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Stem Cell Research: From Biological Data to Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Stem cell (SC) research plays a central role in disease modeling and regenerative medicine, yet its clinical translation remains challenged by biological heterogeneity, incomplete cellular maturation, stringent quality-control requirements, and increasingly complex biological and clinical data. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a powerful computational approach for extracting biologically meaningful information from these data, enabling quantitative characterization of SC behavior and predictive modeling across diverse experimental and translational applications. This review presents a unif
papers.summary: This review surveys how machine learning is being applied across stem cell research, from analyzing complex biological data to supporting clinical translation. It highlights how ML helps address challenges like cellular heterogeneity, incomplete maturation, and quality control by enabling quantitative characterization and predictive modeling of stem cell behavior.

papers.title: Bio-Inspired Artificial Intelligence Multimorbidity Score for Human-Machine Clinical Risk Stratification.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity is strongly associated with mortality, but existing comorbidity indices often generalize poorly across populations because they depend on fixed disease lists and context-specific weights. We developed the large-language-model-based multimorbidity score (LLM-MMS), a prompt-based large-language-model-derived multimorbidity phenotype score, as a bio-inspired artificial intelligence score for human-machine clinical risk stratification and evaluated it for all-cause mortality prediction in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts. Harmonized participant-level data wer
papers.summary: The authors developed LLM-MMS, a prompt-based large language model-derived multimorbidity score designed to predict all-cause mortality across diverse populations. They evaluated it in 770,439 adults from 9 international longitudinal cohorts, aiming to overcome the poor generalizability of fixed disease-list comorbidity indices. The score is framed as a bio-inspired AI tool for human-machine clinical risk stratification.
